name: motion-number-upvotes
title: Animated Upvote Counter
description: A small rounded card showing an upvote total between two round arrow buttons. Clicking up or down rolls the number and tints the card and the chosen button green or red.
use: A post, comment or feature needs a lightweight up and down vote control with an animated score.
avoid: It only changes local state with no undo or persistence, and the colours are fixed to green and red.
a11y: Both arrow controls are icon-only with no aria-labels, so screen readers announce them as unlabelled buttons. (keyboard: yes, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A compact rounded card with bold light text reading 14 Upvotes above two black circular buttons, one holding an up arrow and one a down arrow. It sits on black; pressing an arrow turns the card deep green or deep red.
behaves: Pressing an arrow nudges the number up or down with a vertical rolling animation inside the total. The card background and the pressed button switch to green for up or red for down, and each button shrinks a little while held.
customise: The starting count and the green and red colours are hardcoded and it takes no props; wiring it to real data means editing the component.
weight: light: Two buttons and one number with a short spring; no canvas or loop.
demo: The count starts at 14 and changes to 16 or 15 during the clip.
issues: The arrow buttons have no accessible labels, so their purpose is not announced.
Frames 3 and 5 catch the digits overlapping mid-roll, which reads as a glitch in a still.
polishWhy: Readable count and clear green and red feedback, but the layout and styling are plain.
